notes: Phase B3 of the Python MCP server port — Tasks 4 and 5 from .kiro/specs/python-mcp-server-port/tasks.md: GGSR traversal engine and SDD session manager. Task 3 was a checkpoint (skipped; Tasks 1 and 2 already committed at 4e235d4 and dc293c0 on develop_aws). All code under mcp_server_python/. mcp_server_node/ untouched. No deployments, no ECR pushes, no AgentCore Runtime updates. Side-carried session file (active_session.json is phase56, unrelated).

completedSteps.name: Task 4.1 — Implement src/graphrag/ggsr_traversal.py
completedSteps.notes: 387 lines. GGSRTraversal class with WEIGHT_MATRIX (9 edge types per spec: CALLS=1.0, IMPORTS=0.9, DEFINES=0.85, USES=0.8, EXECUTES=0.95, INVOKES=0.9, SOURCES=0.85, CONTAINS=0.7, DEPENDS_ON=0.75), HOP_DECAY=0.6, DEFAULT_WEIGHT=0.3 for unknown edges. GGSRScoredResult dataclass. Methods: budget_aware_neighborhood (1- or 2-hop, injectable GraphDBProtocol), _score_results (score = weight × HOP_DECAY^hop, sort desc), _trim_to_budget (greedy prefix), _multi_hop_query (Neptune-compatible Cypher: toLower($baseName) CONTAINS, no regex). Node.js GGSRTraversalPrototypes.js uses a larger weight matrix (27 types with different values and HOP_DECAY=0.5); the spec explicitly lists the 9 values and HOP_DECAY=0.6 used here — spec authority wins. Exported via src/graphrag/__init__.py.

completedSteps.name: Task 4.2 — Implement src/graphrag/graph_guided_retrieval.py
completedSteps.notes: 284 lines. GraphGuidedRetrieval(ggsr, vector_db) combining GGSR traversal with OpenSearch vector search. get_code_context() runs graph neighbourhood + semantic enrichment in parallel via asyncio.gather (equivalent to Promise.all in Node.js). Returns GGSRRetrievalResult(entity, ggsr_results, semantic_hits, metadata). Degrades gracefully when vector_db is None (semantic_available=False flag). retrieve = alias of get_code_context for Node.js parity. Community summaries and query classification from the full JS version are deferred to Phase B7 (GraphRAGTools port) per the tasks.md staging.

completedSteps.name: Task 4.3 — Property tests for GGSR (Property 9: scoring correctness)
completedSteps.notes: tests/properties/test_ggsr_props.py, 294 lines, 11 tests. Property 9 is decomposed into: (a) exact score = weight × HOP_DECAY^hop for known edges (150 examples), (b) output sorted by score descending, (c) unknown relationships fall back to DEFAULT_WEIGHT, (d) hop-2 scores decay monotonically from hop-1 for the same edge, (e) trim never exceeds token_budget, (f) trim is a prefix of the sorted list (no reordering), (g) larger budget keeps at least as many rows, (h) all known edges produce finite scores in (0, 1]. Plus edge-case unit tests: empty input, zero budget, hop_distance<1 clamped to 1. Hypothesis strategies: sampled_from(WEIGHT_MATRIX.keys()) + unknown labels, ASCII names, hops ∈ {1, 2}, budgets ∈ [0, 10000].

completedSteps.name: Task 5.1 — Implement src/sdd/session_manager.py
completedSteps.notes: 814 lines. SessionManager class with configurable state_dir, clock, id_factory (all dependency-injected for testability — defaults match the Node.js path convention and Math.random().toString(36).substr(2, 6) ID shape). Data models as dataclasses: SDDSession, SDDStep, FileModification, ExaminedSymbol, Checkpoint (camelCase fields for byte-compat with Node.js active_session.json). Constants: VALID_TAGS, VALID_CHANGE_TYPES, STATUS_ACTIVE/COMPLETED/ABANDONED. Lifecycle: start_session/record_step/complete_session/abandon_session/resume_session. State tracking: examine_symbol (dedup, silent on no-session), mark_modified (appends every call), checkpoint_state (snapshot to checkpoints/<id>.json), restore_checkpoint (reverts examined + modifications). Readers: get_session_state, get_session_context, get_history with phase/event/limit filters. Static serialize_session/deserialize_session for Property 11. threading.Lock guards all disk mutations (FastMCP may run handlers on a thread pool; Node.js was single-threaded). Event names match Node.js history.jsonl: started / step_completed / file_modified / symbol_examined / checkpoint_created / checkpoint_restored / completed / abandoned / resumed.

completedSteps.name: Task 5.2 — Property tests for SDD (Property 10 + Property 11)
completedSteps.notes: tests/properties/test_sdd_session_props.py, 370 lines, 4 property tests × up to 60 Hypothesis examples each. Property 10 (state consistency): (a) examined reflects unique symbols in first-seen order (dedup verified), (b) modifications reflects every mark_modified call with duplicates preserved (same file modified twice appears twice), (c) restore_checkpoint reverts examined + modifications to the snapshot state for any mix of pre/post operations. Property 11 (lifecycle round-trip): start → record N ∈ [0, 6] steps with tags from VALID_TAGS → complete/abandon/stay-active → serialize_session → deserialize_session yields equivalent dict, with phase/totalSteps/completedSteps all preserved. Also validates serialized form is parseable JSON with the required top-level keys. Uses injected deterministic _FakeClock and _id_factory_for_tests to keep Hypothesis shrinks reproducible. Key gotcha resolved: initial function-scoped manager fixture was reused across all Hypothesis examples, so the second example saw the leaked active session from the first. Fixed by inlining _fresh_manager() + tempfile.TemporaryDirectory per iteration in a try/finally — no shared state across examples.

completedSteps.name: Task 5.3 — Unit tests for session manager
completedSteps.notes: tests/unit/test_session_manager.py, 538 lines, 37 tests. Coverage: initialization (state dir created recursively, checkpoints subdir created, no-active-session reads); start_session (file written with Node.js-compatible JSON shape, history event emitted, double-start rejected with SessionError, empty phase_name rejected); record_step (append to completedSteps, currentStep watermark, duplicate step rejected, no-session raises, unknown tag accepted with log warning, empty tag defaults to 'implement', history event emitted); examine_symbol (deduplicates, returns None silently when no session, matches Node.js recordExamined); mark_modified (every call appended even for same path, requires file_path, warns on unknown changeType); checkpoint_state (snapshot written to checkpoints/<id>.json with modifications + examined + currentStep + completedSteps copies, summary entry pushed into session); restore_checkpoint (reverts examined + modifications, unknown id raises); complete_session (status + completedAt set, active file removed, completed event with duration); abandon_session (status + abandonReason set, active file removed); resume_session (across fresh manager instance — simulates server restart — error when no session); JSONL parity (7-event lifecycle sequence is started → step_completed → file_modified → symbol_examined → checkpoint_created → checkpoint_restored → completed with sessionId + phase + timestamp(Z) on every event); active_session.json top-level keys match Node.js; optional lifecycle fields (completedAt, abandonedAt, summary, abandonReason) omitted until transition; get_history event / phase-substring / limit filters; serialize/deserialize round-trip, unknown keys ignored for forward-compat, non-object JSON rejected with ValueError; thread safety smoke test (10 threads concurrently call record_step, final state has exactly steps 1..10 with no corruption). Run summary: 98/98 passed in full suite (57 pre-existing + 41 new across Tasks 4 and 5). No regressions.

followUps: Task 6 (checkpoint) — validate core engine. User should review before proceeding.
Tasks 7+ belong to subsequent phases (B4 parity framework, then B5–B11 tool modules).

Property 9 currently exercises _score_results / _trim_to_budget directly; Phase B7 (GraphRAGTools) will need an end-to-end test of budget_aware_neighborhood against a mock Neptune adapter when the GGSRRetrieval is wired into get_code_context.

Current WEIGHT_MATRIX contains 9 edge types per spec. Node.js GGSRTraversalPrototypes.js has 27 edge types with different values (EXECUTES=1.0 not 0.95, SOURCES=0.95 not 0.85, DEPENDS_ON=0.8 not 0.75) and HOP_DECAY=0.5 not 0.6. If parity tests in Phase B7 reveal score divergence, decide whether to (a) extend WEIGHT_MATRIX + bump spec, or (b) keep spec values and document the intentional divergence.
